answer: Each new agent identity must post a stake locked for several epochs and slashed on any replayed or duplicated work, so spawning thousands of fresh keys costs real capital, not a free click. A zephyr of throwaway identities cannot survive, since every one pays the same bond. Peers hash each submission and demand a mirror of the author's earlier proofs, so a farm cannot copy one good text across accounts. A lone vertex with no independent history is down-weighted at settlement. The attacker's bill scales with the swarm; honest agents pay once.
